title: Check and fix a workload's prerequisites for PIM Manager
purpose: Check, and fix, the prerequisites of ONE workload PIM Manager delegates into (Defender XDR, Intune, Power BI, Azure roles, Entra roles) that PIM cannot fix itself.
whenToRun: When a prerequisite chip in PIM Manager (template cards, the workload wizards, Coverage & gaps) shows this command for a workload, with your environment's values filled in. PIM checks every prerequisite an API can answer itself every day; this script is for what needs a person with more rights than the engine has. Safe to run again: what is already in place is reported and left alone.

runAs.name: delegated Microsoft Graph scopes Application.Read.All and AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All, plus per workload: RoleManagement.Read.Defender (DefenderXdr), DeviceManagementRBAC.Read.All (Intune), Group.ReadWrite.All and GroupMember.ReadWrite.All (PowerBI), Organization.Read.All (EntraRoles)
runAs.scope: the browser sign-in (first-party public client 'Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools')
runAs.why: What the browser sign-in asks for, for the checks and the fixes of the chosen workload only. A check the caller cannot read (for example without Directory.Read.All, or LicenseAssignment.Read.All for the licence list) is reported as NOT CHECKED, never as passed.

runAs.name: delegated Azure access (user_impersonation) through the first-party public client 'Microsoft Azure PowerShell'
runAs.scope: Azure Resource Manager, plus Fabric (PowerBI) and the store (with -SqlServerFqdn) from the same sign-in
runAs.why: Needed for DefenderXdr (Sentinel), AzureRbac, PowerBI (Fabric tenant setting), to find the engine identity from the hosted tick job, and to record the result in the store.

runAs.name: Privileged Role Administrator
runAs.why: Granting the engine a missing Graph application permission (DefenderXdr: RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Defender; Intune: DeviceManagementRBAC.ReadWrite.All; EntraRoles: the engine's Graph role map) needs a Privileged Role Administrator or a Global Administrator.

runAs.name: Groups Administrator
runAs.why: Creates the Power BI admin-API security group and adds the engine identity to it (a User Administrator works too).

runAs.name: Fabric Administrator
runAs.why: Reads and changes the Fabric tenant setting 'Service principals can access read-only admin APIs'. Without it the check is NOT CHECKED and the portal step is shown.

runAs.name: User Access Administrator
runAs.scope: each Azure scope in your delegation rows and -AzureScope (AzureRbac with -GrantAzureUserAccessAdministrator only; Owner works too)
runAs.why: Assigns User Access Administrator to the engine identity at that scope.

runAs.name: Contributor
runAs.scope: the subscription of the dedicated Sentinel workspace (DefenderXdr with -EnableSentinel only)
runAs.why: Creates the dedicated Log Analytics workspace, registers the Microsoft.OperationsManagement and Microsoft.SecurityInsights resource providers and enables Microsoft Sentinel on it.

runAs.name: Reader
runAs.scope: the hosting resource group and the Log Analytics workspaces
runAs.why: Finds the engine identity from the tick job when -EngineObjectId is not given, and reads whether Sentinel is enabled.

runAs.name: Security Administrator
runAs.why: Not used by the script: the script reports the portal step 'activate the Unified RBAC workloads', which a Security Administrator does in the Microsoft Defender portal.

runAs.name: member of the environment's SQL admin group (only to record the result with -SqlServerFqdn)
runAs.why: Without it nothing is recorded here; press Check again in PIM Manager and PIM records it itself.

changes.object: application permission for the engine identity (app role assignment on Microsoft Graph, POST servicePrincipals/{engine}/appRoleAssignments) -- only the ones missing; a role is granted only when the role map's id is the live id
changes.permission: DefenderXdr: RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Defender; Intune: DeviceManagementRBAC.ReadWrite.All; EntraRoles: the engine's full Graph role map (repository runs only)
changes.why: The engine assigns the Defender / Intune / Entra roles you delegate through these permissions.
changes.undo: Entra admin center > Enterprise applications > the engine identity > Permissions > remove the permission.

changes.object: security group -PowerBiSecurityGroupName (default grp-pim-powerbi-admin-api), only when it does not exist (PowerBI)
changes.why: Microsoft's rule for the read-only Power BI admin APIs: the service principal must be in a security group the Fabric tenant setting allows.
changes.undo: Delete the group (first remove it from the Fabric tenant setting).

changes.object: member of the Power BI admin-API security group: the engine identity (PowerBI)
changes.permission: group membership that the Fabric setting 'Service principals can access read-only admin APIs' allows
changes.scope: the Power BI admin-API security group
changes.why: Lets the engine call the read-only Power BI admin APIs to manage Power BI workspace access.
changes.undo: Remove the engine identity from the group.

changes.object: tenant setting 'Service principals can access read-only admin APIs' (AllowServicePrincipalsUseReadAdminAPIs): enabled for the group, every group already in it kept (PowerBI)
changes.why: Without it the engine's Power BI admin API calls are refused.
changes.undo: Fabric admin portal > Tenant settings > Admin API settings > remove the group (or disable the setting if the script enabled it).

changes.object: Azure role assignment for the engine identity (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments) at each scope it is missing (AzureRbac, OPT-IN with -GrantAzureUserAccessAdministrator)
changes.permission: User Access Administrator (an Owner or User Access Administrator already held there counts; Reader and Role Based Access Control Administrator are reported, not granted)
changes.scope: each Azure scope in your PIM-Assignments-Azure-Resources rows and -AzureScope
changes.why: The engine assigns the Azure resource roles you delegate. It is standing privilege, so it is opt-in.
changes.undo: Azure portal > the scope > Access control (IAM) > remove the engine identity's User Access Administrator assignment.

changes.object: dedicated Log Analytics workspace law-sentinel-<suffix> (PerGB2018, 30 days) in -ResourceGroup, or -SentinelWorkspaceId; never PIM's own log workspace (DefenderXdr, OPT-IN with -EnableSentinel; billed per GB ingested)
changes.why: Defender Data Operations roles need Microsoft Sentinel on a workspace.
changes.undo: Delete the workspace (and its Sentinel solution).

changes.object: resource provider registration Microsoft.OperationsManagement and Microsoft.SecurityInsights on the workspace's subscription, when not registered (-EnableSentinel)
changes.why: Sentinel cannot be enabled without them.
changes.undo: Unregister the providers (only when nothing else in the subscription uses them).

changes.object: Microsoft Sentinel on the workspace (Microsoft.SecurityInsights onboardingStates/default) (-EnableSentinel)
changes.why: Defender Data Operations roles need Microsoft Sentinel on a workspace.
changes.undo: Remove Microsoft Sentinel from the workspace (Microsoft Sentinel > Settings > Remove Microsoft Sentinel).

changes.object: pim.Settings 'WorkloadPrereqs': this workload's result merged in (a confirmation made in PIM Manager is kept), read back and audited -- only with -SqlServerFqdn and access to the store
changes.why: PIM Manager shows the result on the template cards and Coverage & gaps.
changes.undo: Press Check again in PIM Manager: PIM records its own result.

parameters.name: Workload
parameters.help: DefenderXdr, Intune, PowerBI, AzureRbac or EntraRoles.

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: Your tenant id; every sign-in and token is checked against it.

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The hosting subscription (finds the engine identity from the tick job; holds the dedicated Sentinel workspace).

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: The hosting resource group.

parameters.name: TickJobName
parameters.help: The engine's job (its identity is the engine identity when -EngineObjectId is not given).

parameters.name: SqlServerFqdn
parameters.help: The environment's store; without it (or access to it) the result is not recorded here.

parameters.name: SqlDatabase
parameters.help: The store's database.

parameters.name: ClientId
parameters.help: Automation from the repository only: a certificate identity (with -CertThumbprint). Never shown by PIM Manager.

parameters.name: CertThumbprint
parameters.help: Automation from the repository only: the certificate of -ClientId.

parameters.name: UseSignedInAccount
parameters.help: Use the signed-in session of this window (the Invardia Support app session opened by Invardia's connect script; without one, your own browser sign-in).

parameters.name: UseEdge
parameters.help: $true opens Microsoft Edge for the sign-in; $false the default browser.

parameters.name: EngineObjectId
parameters.help: The engine identity's object id (shown in PIM Manager).

parameters.name: EngineAppId
parameters.help: The engine application's id, instead of -EngineObjectId.

parameters.name: EngineCertThumbprint
parameters.help: Only with an engine application whose certificate is on this computer: test the Power BI admin API as the engine.

parameters.name: ConfirmPortalStep
parameters.help: Check ids of portal steps you have done; recorded as confirmed (attested, not verified).

parameters.name: SkipDataOperations
parameters.help: DefenderXdr: skip the Data Operations / Sentinel checks.

parameters.name: SentinelWorkspaceId
parameters.help: DefenderXdr: the Log Analytics workspace to check (and, with -EnableSentinel, enable).

parameters.name: EnableSentinel
parameters.help: DefenderXdr, OPT-IN (billed per GB ingested): enable Microsoft Sentinel on a dedicated workspace.

parameters.name: PowerBiSecurityGroupName
parameters.help: PowerBI: the admin-API security group.

parameters.name: AzureScope
parameters.help: AzureRbac: more Azure scopes to check.

parameters.name: GrantAzureUserAccessAdministrator
parameters.help: AzureRbac, OPT-IN: assign User Access Administrator to the engine where it is missing.

readsOnly: the engine identity and its application permissions; Microsoft Graph's and the Power BI Service's service principals
Defender Unified RBAC role definitions and the permission catalog; the Log Analytics workspaces (Azure Resource Graph) and their Sentinel state
Intune role definitions; the tenant's licences (AAD_PREMIUM_P2)
the Power BI admin-API group and its members; the Fabric tenant settings
the engine's Azure role assignments at each scope; the delegation rows in the store (AzureRbac)
the stored result in pim.Settings 'WorkloadPrereqs' (to merge)
network: localhost (the browser returns the sign-in to a local port on this computer)
whatIf: Signs in, runs every check of the workload, and prints one "What if:" line per fix it would make (grant a Graph application permission, create the Power BI group, add the engine to it, enable the Fabric setting, assign User Access Administrator, create the Sentinel workspace, register the providers, enable Sentinel). A fix that depends on an earlier one not made yet says it cannot be previewed. Nothing is changed and nothing is recorded; the exit code is 0.
undo: Reverse each change listed above: remove the engine's new application permissions and Azure role assignments, remove the engine from the Power BI group (or delete the group), take the group out of the Fabric setting, and remove Sentinel / the dedicated workspace if the script created them.
